body:
## Adjacent, not duplicate — #16781

Cross-linking rather than closing: #16781 (`finding(runtime): scoped /api/v1/environments/:id/packages[/:id] has no dispatcher door on a plugin-hono-server-only composition after #16628`) is a sibling of this card on the same surface, and both are #16628 residue, but they are different defects:

- **#16781 is a MOUNT gap** — on a `plugin-hono-server` + REST composition without `createHonoApp`, the scoped package path has no door at all after the REST mirror was removed, so the transport's bare `notFound` answers.
- **This card is a PARAMETER-READ gap** on the door that *does* exist — where the dispatcher is reached, it serves the route and answers `200`, having silently ignored `?version=`.

They do not overlap in remedy: restoring a scoped mount does not make the handler read `version`, and making the handler read `version` does not give a door to a composition that has none. A seat taking either should know the other exists, since both land in the same `/packages` domain branch and a repair to one is a natural place to notice the other.

Noted while implementing #12034, whose PR (#17419) binds the response type for this same route.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**Triage: `finding` admitted as class (c); lands on `GET /api/v1/packages/:id`; `domain:cli`; `priority:p2`.**

The route **accepts a `?version=` query parameter from the SDK** and **the only surface that serves it never reads it**. The caller is answered **`200` with the installed version**, and **nothing in the status, headers or body distinguishes that from a version-scoped response**.

⇒ p2, and the reason is the `200`. ⭐ A silently-ignored parameter that still returns success is the worst answer available: the caller believes it received the version it asked for, and there is **no signal anywhere in the response** to tell it otherwise. A 400 would be honest; even a header would be. This is neither.

⇒ ⚠️ **Two exits, pick deliberately:** honour `?version=`, or **refuse it** so the caller knows. ⛔ Silently ignoring is not a third option. ⚠️ If honouring it is out of reach (the handler that did was deleted with the REST twin), then **refuse and say so in the error** — and say in the PR what the SDK should do instead.

⚠️ **Check the SDK side**: it *sends* the parameter, so whichever exit is chosen, the SDK's expectation has to match or the refusal lands on our own client first.

⛔ Not in scope: #12034's response-shape work, correctly fenced.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

## fold-or-serial, answered explicitly

This card and **#17432** are both `packages/runtime` p2s dispatched in the same wave, so the answer is owed: **SERIAL / separate, ⛔ NOT folded.** Gate ① fails outright — they are different defects with different remedies in different files. Triage drew the same distinction on this very card against #16781: 「restoring a scoped mount does not make the handler read `version`, and making the handler read `version` does not give a door to a …」. Gate ③ also fails: #17432 carries an **escalation condition** that could re-price it to p1 on the security floor, and a card that might be a security finding is ⛔ never folded with an unrelated one.

## Zone 1 — RULING, with a named premise and a hard stop

### ① Ruling (⛔ not re-openable)

**A silently-ignored parameter answered `200` is not an acceptable end state.** Triage's framing is adopted verbatim: 「honour `?version=`, or **refuse it** so the caller knows. ⛔ Silently ignoring is not a third option.」 The SDK *declares* `version?: string` and sends it, so this is a **declared-but-unenforced** capability — and this repo's first commandment is that a declaration the runtime does not honour is the shape to eliminate, ⛔ not to document.

### ② The premise — ⭐ measure it FIRST, and it selects the exit

**Premise: honouring is reachable.** If the registry can serve a version-scoped read, **honour `?version=`** — that is a `packages/runtime`-only change, it makes a declared capability real, and it needs ⛔ no SDK change.

Two readings I took that make this worth trying before concluding it is out of reach:
- `handlePackagesRequest` (`domains/packages.ts:534`) **already receives `query`** and already uses it on sibling branches — `:577` `query?.status`, `:580` `query?.type`, `:635` `query?.overwrite`. ⇒ 「the handler cannot see the parameter」 is **false**; it is threaded and in use a few branches away.
- The GET-by-id branch is at **`:1211`** (`parts.length === 1 && m === 'GET'`), and it reads the path id only. ⚠️ **Re-locate it** — `#17433` touched this exact file most recently (「reconcile its read/delete responses to the spec」), so coordinates may have moved.

### ③ The hard stop — ⛔ do NOT take the other exit on your own

If you measure that honouring is genuinely out of reach (the version-scoped read went with the REST twin in **#16628** and the registry cannot express it), then the remaining exit is **refuse**. ⛔ **STOP and report a fork — do not implement it.** The reason is mechanical, not aesthetic:

> triage's own warning: 「it *sends* the parameter, so whichever exit is chosen, **the SDK's expectation has to match or the refusal lands on our own client first**」

⇒ refusing server-side requires changing `packages/client/src/index.ts`, and that file is **hard-serial behind PR #17454 this round**. ⛔ Refusing while leaving the SDK sending it would break our own client — the exact outcome triage flagged. ⇒ `status: needs_decision`, `pr: null`, non-empty `open_questions` is a **full delivery** here, and I will either re-dispatch it once #17454 merges or file the pairing. ⛔ Do not widen onto the fenced file, and ⛔ do not settle for a header or a warning log as a compromise — that is the third option the ruling forbids.

## Zone 3 — SUGGESTED ROUTE (optional; measurement outranks it)

On the `:1211` branch, read `query?.version` and serve the version-scoped package when it is present. ⚠️ **Say explicitly what happens when the requested version does not exist** — a `404` and a `200`-with-the-installed-version are very different answers, and the second is the defect this card is about, one layer in.

## Acceptance — one named, independently checkable criterion

`GET /api/v1/packages/:id?version=<v>` must **stop being indistinguishable** from the unversioned read. Pin the pair: a request **with** `?version=` pointing at a non-installed version, and the **same** request without it, must not produce the same response. ⭐ **Minimum assertions are `status` + the discriminating field** — ⛔ never 「it returned 200」, which is precisely the reading that hid this defect.

⭐ Include the lit control: an unversioned `GET /api/v1/packages/:id` still answers exactly as it does today. A green that only exercises the new path would also pass if you broke the ordinary read.

## Gates

Derive from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands <your ACTUAL changed paths>` on your **final** diff (⛔ re-derive). Redirect each and capture `$?` **before** any pipe; reconcile with `--ran`. Read hit **lines**, ⛔ never counts. This lane always adds **`pnpm lint`**. A changeset is owed unless `skip-changeset` genuinely applies — decide explicitly.

⚠️ Heavy runs go through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` with your own `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT`. A sibling is building right now; an **exit 99 queue-timeout is NOT MEASURED, ⛔ not a failure** — record it, spend the interval on lock-free work, and retake under the same slot.

## Report

`os-dev-report` as an issue comment **first**, then the return message; machine-checkable fields only (`gates` / `line_budget` / `deviations` / `files_changed`). ⛔ Do not re-narrate the PR body. Draft PR, target `main`, first line `Fixes #17416`.

⛔ **Do not write a second claim comment** — this one is your identity. If the newest claim on this card does not name your branch, stop and report.
